courseTitle: The History of Australia: First Nations, Colonisation & Resistance (1770–1901)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 3 Curriculum Knowledge & Revision Mind Map.

root.label: Australia, 1770–1901
root.gloss: First Nations custodianship, British colonisation, frontier resistance, the Gold Rush, and the long struggle from terra nullius to Mabo.

children.label: Part 1: Claim & Penal Colony
children.gloss: Cook’s Pacific voyage with Tupaia, the British claim of terra nullius, and the founding of the Sydney Cove convict colony.

children.label: 1. Cook, Tupaia & Terra Nullius
children.gloss: Secret Admiralty orders, Tupaia’s star navigation, the Gweagal encounter at Botany Bay, and the legal fiction of terra nullius.

children.label: Cook’s Orders & Tupaia’s Chart
children.gloss: Cook carried secret Admiralty orders for Terra Australis while Tahitian high priest Tupaia guided HMS Endeavour across the Pacific.

children.label: Secret Orders for Southern Land
children.gloss: Funded to observe Venus transit; Ordered to claim Terra Australis.

children.label: Tupaia Mapped 130 Pacific Islands
children.gloss: Read stars, swells, bird paths; Translated for Māori in NZ.

children.label: → Guided Endeavour to East Coast
children.gloss: Reached Botany Bay April 1770; Surveyed uncharted Pacific safely.

children.label: Polynesian Skill Enabled Voyage
children.gloss: European charts lacked Pacific routes; Indigenous priest proved indispensable.

children.label: Botany Bay & Possession Island
children.gloss: Gweagal warriors defended Botany Bay against armed landing parties before Cook claimed eastern Australia on Possession Island.

children.label: Gweagal Warriors Defended Shore
children.gloss: Two Dharawal men shouted warnings; Cook’s musket wounded warrior’s leg.

children.label: Union Jack on Possession Island
children.gloss: Landed off Cape York August; Claimed east coast for George III.

children.label: Claimed east coast for George III
children.gloss: Claimed east coast for George III

children.label: → Seized Coast Without Consent
children.gloss: Broke explicit Admiralty consent rule; Ignored clear Indigenous habitation.

children.label: Planted Flag Through Armed Force
children.gloss: Treated spear protocol as aggression; Set violent pattern of contact.

children.label: Legal Fiction of Terra Nullius
children.gloss: British jurists declared Australia terra nullius ("nobody’s land"), signing zero treaties and stripping First Nations of land rights.

children.label: European Plough & Fence Law
children.gloss: Cook called clans non-farming nomads; Law required fences and towns.

children.label: Declared Continent Nobody’s Land
children.gloss: Recognised zero Indigenous ownership; Signed no treaties with elders.

children.label: → Cleared Legal Path for Penal Fleet
children.gloss: Justified 1788 British settlement; Stripped clans of ancestral sovereignty.

children.label: Two Centuries of Dispossession
children.gloss: Denied basic legal land rights; Stood in law until 1992.

children.label: 2. First Fleet & Sydney Cove
children.gloss: American independence overcrowded Thames prison hulks, prompting Arthur Phillip’s First Fleet and the harsh struggle at Sydney Cove.

children.label: Thames Hulks & First Fleet
children.gloss: Losing America closed Britain’s convict outlet, filling rotting Thames hulks until Pitt dispatched Phillip’s 11-ship First Fleet.

children.label: 1783 American Loss & Hulks Crisis
children.gloss: Closed American plantation convict route; Typhus raged inside Thames hulks.

children.label: Phillip Sailed 11-Ship Convoy
children.gloss: Over 750 convicts, 250 marines; Sailed 15,000 miles eight months.

children.label: → Reached Botany Bay With Low Loss
children.gloss: Clean water and ship ventilation; Fewer than fifty convicts died.

children.label: Exported Britain’s Prison Crisis
children.gloss: Pitt chose distant Botany Bay; Built empire through penal labour.

children.label: Sydney Cove & Starvation Years
children.gloss: Phillip rejected swampy Botany Bay for Port Jackson, but sandy soil, snapped hoes, and shipwreck pushed Sydney near starvation.

children.label: Moved Settlement to Sydney Cove
children.gloss: Rejected swampy shallow Botany Bay; Raised flag 26 January 1788.

children.label: Sandy Soil & Guardian Shipwreck
children.gloss: Urban convicts lacked farm skills; HMS Guardian struck Antarctic iceberg.

children.label: → Ration Cuts & Inland Farm Push
children.gloss: Phillip slashed rations to survive; Sent convicts to Norfolk Island.

children.label: Hardship Threatened Colony Survival
children.gloss: Tools snapped on eucalyptus roots; English seed failed in sand.

children.label: Convict Lash & Emancipist Farms
children.gloss: Phillip combined brutal cat-o’-nine-tails discipline with 30-acre land grants for freed emancipists such as James Ruse.

children.label: Open-Air Prison & Brutal Lash
children.gloss: Quarried stone dawn to dusk; Flogged with cat-o’-nine-tails lash.

children.label: 30-Acre Grants for Emancipists
children.gloss: Rewarded convicts finishing sentences; James Ruse grew Rose Hill wheat.

children.label: James Ruse grew Rose Hill wheat
children.gloss: James Ruse grew Rose Hill wheat

children.label: → Expanded Farms Into Eora Country
children.gloss: Secured colonial food supply; Cleared bush along river valleys.

children.label: Brutal Jail vs Emancipist Chance
children.gloss: Harsh floggings enforced forced labour; Land grants built settler society.

children.label: Part 2: Frontier Wars & Wool
children.gloss: Smallpox devastation, Bennelong’s diplomacy, Pemulwuy’s guerrilla war, Tasmania’s Black War, and the Myall Creek trial.

children.label: 3. Smallpox, Bennelong & Pemulwuy
children.gloss: 65,000 years of First Nations custodianship collided with the 1789 smallpox epidemic, Bennelong’s captivity, and Pemulwuy’s resistance.

children.label: 65,000 Years & 1789 Smallpox
children.gloss: Over 250 language nations managed country for 65,000 years before the April 1789 gal-galla smallpox outbreak killed 50–70% of Eora.

children.label: 250+ Nations & Fire-Stick Care
children.gloss: 65,000 years continuous civilisation; Songlines and controlled grass burning.

children.label: 1789 Smallpox Killed 50–70% Eora
children.gloss: Zero natural immunity to virus; Lost elders and sacred law.

children.label: → Weakened Clans as Settlers Spread
children.gloss: Shattered coastal clan social bonds; Eased British seizure of creeks.

children.label: Amity Myth vs Frontier Catastrophe
children.gloss: Old histories stressed peaceful contact; Evidence shows disease and war.

children.label: Bennelong’s Tragic Diplomacy
children.gloss: Kidnapped Wangal warrior Bennelong mediated between Eora clans and Governor Phillip and visited London, ending trapped between worlds.

children.label: Phillip Kidnapped Wangal Mediator
children.gloss: Seized by marines late 1789; Learned English at Government House.

children.label: London Voyage & Met George III
children.gloss: Sailed with Phillip in 1792; Negotiated early Sydney clan meetings.

children.label: → Diplomacy Collapsed Over Land Theft
children.gloss: Returned alienated from both sides; Settler farms sparked armed resistance.

children.label: Symbolised Tragic Cultural Divide
children.gloss: Sought peace through personal diplomacy; Crushed by relentless land seizure.

children.label: Pemulwuy & Hawkesbury War
children.gloss: Bidjigal warrior Pemulwuy led guerrilla raids and fought at Parramatta (1797) until Governor King’s shoot-on-sight orders ended in ambush.

children.label: Pemulwuy’s Guerrilla Raids & 1797
children.gloss: Burned settler farms and grain; Survived wounds after Parramatta raid.

children.label: Hawkesbury War & Shoot-on-Sight
children.gloss: Farms seized Dharug yam beds; Governor King outlawed Indigenous men.

children.label: → 1802 Ambush Ended First War
children.gloss: Pemulwuy killed in 1802 ambush; Severed head shipped to London.

children.label: Proved Organised Armed Resistance
children.gloss: United clans across Sydney Basin; Refuted myth of passive surrender.

children.label: 4. Black War & Myall Creek
children.gloss: Invasion of Van Diemen’s Land, Governor Arthur’s Black Line, Truganini’s exile, mainland Merino wool expansion, and Myall Creek.

children.label: Tasmania’s Black War & Black Line
children.gloss: Risdon Cove killings and sheep expansion sparked Palawa guerrilla resistance, Governor Arthur’s 1828 martial law, and the failed Black Line.

children.label: Risdon Cove & Midlands Sheep Grab
children.gloss: 1804 cannon fired on Palawa; Pastoralists seized kangaroo hunting land.

children.label: 1828 Martial Law & Black Line
children.gloss: 2,200 men swept island south; £30,000 drive caught two people.

children.label: → Turned to Robinson’s Exile Plan
children.gloss: Palawa slipped past army cordon; Military failure forced diplomatic ploy.

children.label: Deadliest Colonial Frontier Conflict
children.gloss: Allowed shooting Palawa on sight; Devastated island’s 6,000 Indigenous people.

children.label: Truganini & Wybalenna Exile
children.gloss: Missionary George Augustus Robinson used Truganini’s diplomacy to persuade surviving Palawa into tragic exile on Flinders Island.

children.label: Truganini’s Peacemaking Diplomacy
children.gloss: Enlisted by missionary George Robinson; Sought safety for surviving clans.

children.label: 200 Exiled to Flinders Island
children.gloss: Betrayed promise of mainland return; Held in damp Wybalenna camp.

children.label: → Over 150 Died Within Decade
children.gloss: Struck by sickness and grief; Near-destruction of Palawa communities.

children.label: Enduring Symbol of Palawa Survival
children.gloss: Truganini outlived broken British pledges; Exposed lethality of forced removal.

children.label: Merino Boom & Myall Creek Trial
children.gloss: Mainland squatters drove millions of Merino sheep across Indigenous country, culminating in the 1838 Myall Creek massacre and hangings.

children.label: Yorkshire Wool & Squatter Flocks
children.gloss: Millions of Merino crossed mountains; Sheep ruined native yam fields.

children.label: 28 Wirrayaraay Murdered June 1838
children.gloss: Eleven white stockmen attacked camp; Governor Gipps ordered two trials.

children.label: → Seven Hanged; Settler Code of Silence
children.gloss: Seven white stockmen hanged Sydney; Future massacres hidden in secrecy.

children.label: Rare Colonial Murder Conviction
children.gloss: Provoked furious colonial press outrage; Exception proving wider frontier impunity.

children.label: Part 3: Gold, Votes & Mabo
children.gloss: The 1851 Gold Rush, Ballarat’s Eureka Stockade, anti-Chinese racism, 1901 Federation, and the 1992 Mabo Native Title ruling.

children.label: 5. Gold Rush, Eureka & Mabo
children.gloss: Gold transformed Australia’s wealth and democracy at Eureka, while racial exclusion endured from 1901 until First Nations won Mabo.

children.label: Gold Boom & Licence Hunts
children.gloss: Payable gold at Bathurst, Ballarat, and Bendigo tripled population to 1.2m while 30-shilling licences provoked digger fury.

children.label: 1851 Gold Tripled Colony Population
children.gloss: Hargraves found Bathurst gold 1851; Population jumped to 1.2 million.

children.label: 30-Shilling Monthly Licence Tax
children.gloss: Charged even on empty shafts; Armed police chained unpaid diggers.

children.label: → Bakery Hill Rallies Built Stockade
children.gloss: Protested taxation without any vote; Formed Ballarat Reform League 1854.

children.label: Financed Grand Victorian Melbourne
children.gloss: Half million migrants poured in; Boomed railways and colonial trade.

children.label: Eureka Stockade & Voting Rights
children.gloss: Redcoats crushed the Ballarat diggers’ Eureka Stockade in 15 minutes, but public sympathy forced democratic voting reforms.

children.label: Oath Under Southern Cross Flag
children.gloss: Built wooden stockade at Eureka; Swore to defend civil liberties.

children.label: Dawn Redcoat Assault Killed 22
children.gloss: Three hundred troops stormed camp; Crushed revolt in fifteen minutes.

children.label: → Abolished Fee & Won Suffrage
children.gloss: Scrapped hated monthly mining licence; Introduced secret ballot and suffrage.

children.label: Birthplace of Colonial Democracy
children.gloss: Public outrage backed rebel diggers; Expanded white male voting rights.

children.label: White Australia to 1992 Mabo
children.gloss: Goldfield racism led to the 1901 White Australia Policy and Indigenous exclusion until campaigners won the 1992 Mabo judgement.

children.label: Lambing Flat Anti-Chinese Riots
children.gloss: 40,000 Chinese reworked gold claims; White mobs attacked camps 1861.

children.label: 1901 White Australia & Exclusion
children.gloss: Dictation tests barred non-Europeans; Stolen Generations child removals followed.

children.label: → 1938 Protest to 1992 Mabo Win
children.gloss: 1938 Sydney Day of Mourning; High Court recognised Native Title.

children.label: Mabo Overturned Terra Nullius Myth
children.gloss: Ended 1770 empty continent fiction; Landmark victory for First Nations.
